## Restricted maximum likelihood (REML)

**Problem:** ML estimates of variance components are biased, because we also have to estimate $\boldsymbol{\beta}$

**REML solution:** Write down a new likelihood function for a transformation of $\mathbf{y}$ that does *not* depend on $\boldsymbol{\beta}$

\vspace{6cm}

## REML

## Model assumptions

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Heterozygosity}_{ij} &= \beta_0 + u_i + \beta_1 \log(\text{breeding range}_{ij}) \\ &\hspace{0.5cm} + \beta_2 \log(\text{mass}_{ij}) + \beta_3 \text{latitude}_{ij} + \varepsilon_{ij}
\end{aligned}
$$
$$u_i \overset{iid}{\sim} N(0, \sigma_u^2) \hspace{1cm} \varepsilon_{ij} \overset{iid}{\sim} N(0, \sigma_{\varepsilon}^2)$$

**Question:** What assumptions is this model making?
